how: Moon: NASA LOLA 20 m terrain for all 9 Artemis regions
Earth: 30 m terrain worldwide, bare ground only (no trees, crops)
Cast shadows at sun 1-5°, measure rims and texture, then match
tested: Our Moon shadows vs NASA's own light map: r = 0.98
Known analog beats a decoy 80% of the time (13 known, 9 decoys)
Weights moved ±20%: top-site lists still overlap 88%
new: 33 of the 57 Earth sites we picked for the 9 Moon regions:
No prior analog study found in the catalogs and literature we checked

gaps.d: We match the shape of the ground and how sunlight falls on it, not gravity, vacuum, dust or soil.
Our height maps are too coarse to show boulders and small craters.
Our sites recreate the three dangers, but overall the ground still differs from the Moon’s.

next.d: LRO camera terrain at 2–5 m for the Moon, 1–2 m lidar and ArcticDEM for Earth, so boulders and small craters count.
From a 15% sample to all of Earth’s bare land, refreshed as new satellite data arrives.
Run the same pipeline on Mars landing sites with NASA’s MOLA and HiRISE terrain.

sources: NASA LOLA (PGDA), NASADEM, MODIS, HLS (GIBS) + GLO-30, WorldCover
